thread:
chris: quick q — for the automatic rollout contingency modes, do we have a clear audit surface that ties a triggered contingency to the exact policy + change that caused it?
sara: short answer: partial. we log the action but not a human-friendly diff today. :/
tariq: we log policy_id, policy_version, and reason_code in telemetry. but the UI only shows the policy_id. we should show the diff and who approved it.
lina: +1. ops gets paged with `contingency_trigger` but they can’t tell if it was a config drift or a model performance regression. needs better context.
mike: is the ask: 1) include the policy diff in the incident page, 2) make policy_version immutable and signed, 3) surface the runtime metrics that led to the trigger?
sara: yep. and also retention for those diffs for compliance (90d min).
chris: sketching a small prototype for the API returns we could add: `policy_id`, `policy_version`, `author`, `change_summary`, `diff_url`, `trigger_reason`, `metric_snapshot`. would that cover it?
tariq: sounds good. for `metric_snapshot` we should include `route`, `latency_p95`, `error_rate`, `fallback_count`, `kv_cache_hit_rate`. name fields explicitly so downstream BI can join.
lina: + emoji: :eyes: Also we need to be careful about PII in `change_summary` — it should be structured and avoid freeform user identifiers.
mike: proposal for console UX: in the rollout timeline, next to each contingency event show a small pill with `policy_version` and a link to a read-only snapshot modal that shows the diff and the metric snapshot at trigger time. modal should have an export button (JSON/CSV) and an audit entry with who clicked what.
sara: UI note: modal should also show an action log with `automatic_actions` (e.g., `soft_rollback`, `reroute_to_backup`, `rate_limit`) and the exact parameters. ops wants to copy that into runbooks.
chris: here's a quick example payload we could emit from the runtime when a contingency fires:
```json
{
  "event_ts": 1802201299,
  "policy_id": "cont-42",
  "policy_version": "v3-2026-02-10-17:12",
  "author": "sara",
  "change_summary": "reduced primary pool concurrency; added hedging rule for long tail",
  "diff_url": "https://console.redwood/proj/x/policies/cont-42/v3/diff",
  "trigger_reason": "latency_spike_p95>1200ms",
  "metric_snapshot": { "route": "/chat/generate", "latency_p95": "1.3s", "error_rate": "0.08", "fallback_count": "12" },
  "actions": ["soft_rollback","temporary_route_hedge"]
}
```
sara: love that. a couple things: 1) the runtime needs to sign the payload (HMAC) so we can verify authenticity in the audit log, 2) `metric_snapshot` values should be numeric not strings.
tariq: agreed on HMAC. we should also record `node_id` and `region` to debug capacity-related triggers. and include `seq_id` so duplicates are detectable.
lina: what about policy previews? product wants folks to run a dry-run and see if the policy would have fired historically. we can wire the historical-run results to the same audit UI with a `simulated` flag.
mike: important: simulated events must be clearly marked so they don't trigger billing or SLA alerts. add `simulated: true|false`.
chris: on the retention/export side: compliance asks for an immutable export every time a policy change is promoted to prod. we can push signed blobs to S3 with lifecycle rules and an index doc.
sara: also need an approvals audit: who approved the policy roll and when (for canary/cutover). show that in the modal.
tariq: implementation note: runtime currently emits minimal fields to reduce payload size. adding metric snapshots will increase traffic. maybe we emit a small pointer to a compressed snapshot stored in object storage and the event includes `snapshot_url` + `snapshot_hmac`.
lina: good compromise. console can fetch the snapshot on modal open. show a loading state.
mike: for alerts: should we create a new alert dimension `contingency_origin` with values `policy`, `infrastructure`, `model_regression`? would help reduce noisy pages.
sara: yes. and hook MLOps alerts into `model_regression` so they get routed to the right team.
chris: action items: 1) eng-platform to add `policy_diff_url`, `policy_author`, `snapshot_url`, `snapshot_hmac`, `node_id`, `region`, `seq_id` to runtime event (tariq), 2) console to create read-only modal that can render diff + snapshot + approvals (mike + lina), 3) product to spec `simulated` runs + retention (sara). anyone object?
tariq: no objections. i’ll send a PR with the runtime schema and a lightweight signer util.
mike: i can mock the modal in Figma and link to the PR.
sara: i'll draft the compliance requirements for retention and signature verification.
deploy-bot: "deploy queued: schema-update-runtime-events v0.1 -> staging"
chris: cool. let's keep the convo here as we iterate. thanks all. :rocket:
